name: ambilight-off-leaves-the-space-alone
description:
with the Page tint switch off, the chrome stays on the space's own theme and nothing reads the page at all. Same split fixture its partner ambilight-reads-both-edges measures a varied tint on, so the only difference between the two runs is the setting.

Without that pair this scenario would pass for a build where the whole feature was broken.

actions.note: gate: the sidebar drew. A settle caught an empty sidebar at 9.5s on a slow VM run.
the split page committed, read from the page itself

longer than the whole cadence ladder takes to walk down, had one been running. Before the first capture rather than between the two: this window is glass over the desktop whenever the sidebar has not painted, and that surface drifts about 0.7 a second on its own. Measuring across six seconds of it graded the VM, not the setting.
the same window page-tint-off measures 0.07 across, so this assertion is comparable to its siblings rather than carrying a threshold of its own

assertions.label: the-page-really-loaded
assertions.desc: THE CONTROL: the split page committed, so a sampler that ignored the setting would have had something to read.

assertions.label: nothing-was-sampled
assertions.desc: The readback never ran. The partner scenario logs this line on the same fixture within half a second of the page painting.

assertions.label: no-loop-was-running
assertions.desc: Together: no ladder walked down, because no timer was ticking to walk it. An 'off' that merely skipped the paint would still log this.
THE MEASUREMENT: the sidebar never moved across five seconds of a page the partner scenario reads two different colours off.
assertions.note: The band the glow paints: 32 DIP out from the card's left edge at about x=225 in the VM frame, at 55 percent of the glass alpha. Re-measured 2026-08-27 when the glow was narrowed and dimmed.
